races.name: Kilmore Quay (C & G) Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Plastic Paddy
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type, 21 days fresh, but the fade-in-finish flag and a form string of two pulled-ups makes it very hard to trust at 8yo in a strongly-contested 16-runner maiden.

runners_data.name: Among The Pines
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose natural position is at the rear; a 55-day absence and a sequence of mid-to-back finishes on good ground provide little encouragement, and being pressed into midfield only makes the task harder.

runners_data.name: Chasing Blues
runners_data.note: De Bromhead and Darragh O'Keeffe is a strong combination, and a fourth on good ground over 2m4f hints at some ability; though its natural style is hold-up, it is the most likely of the redistributed group to carve out a useful midfield position.

runners_data.name: Colwyn Bay
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a consistent record of finishing without winning; pulled-up and fell in recent starts, and its genuine hold-up style is compromised by being pushed into midfield against its instincts.

runners_data.name: Drumconnor Hill
runners_data.note: Unknown style from a lightly-raced five-year-old; two hurdles runs both on good ground with a place second last time, so there is something to work with, but the 58-day absence and the U-tag add uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Highland Realm
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner — Mullins-trained, two hurdle runs both on good ground, placed last time, and Sean O'Keeffe takes over; can control the tempo entirely and will be very difficult to pass if allowed a comfortable lead.

runners_data.name: Owl's Delight
runners_data.note: 269 days off the track is an enormous concern; a string of falls, pulls-up and also-rans in recent outings, and the hold-up style will leave it dependent on others setting up a searching pace that seems unlikely today.

runners_data.name: Penny Express
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy adds significant jockey clout for Gordon Elliott; a genuine prominent racer with three career places and consistent good-ground form, well-suited to sitting just off Highland Realm and pouncing at the business end.

runners_data.name: Betterluckthistime
runners_data.note: Four-year-old from the Rothwell yard with only two hurdles starts and a fade-in-finish pattern; the hold-up style means it is effectively racing from further back than its map position suggests.

runners_data.name: Blue Nude
runners_data.note: Another Rothwell inmate, lightly raced, with the worst form figures in the field (8th and 16th); its natural hold-up instinct is squeezed by the redistribution into midfield, making a forward challenge very unlikely.

runners_data.name: Finjimk
runners_data.note: Peter John Flood's four-year-old fell on debut then ran 7th and 8th on good ground; a true hold-up horse operating on the map in midfield, so it is unlikely to see out its natural race shape in this crowded field.

runners_data.name: Game Point
runners_data.note: Consistent form figures of 3-2-3 over hurdles on good ground make this Donagh Meyler-ridden four-year-old one of the more interesting prominent types; hurdle form shows a progressive placing sequence and a headgear note (h) adds an angle.

runners_data.name: Pinkarizon
runners_data.note: Two pulled-ups over hurdles but with flat form suggesting underlying ability; the headgear (ht) change may sharpen focus, but a hold-up style in a field this size with no real pace makes a winning run very hard to construct.

runners_data.name: Plus Or Minus
runners_data.note: Hold-up type stepping up sharply in trip from flat/bumper form on softer ground predominantly; the fade-in-finish flag and step into 2m½f hurdle company make this a very tough assignment for a four-year-old.

runners_data.name: Megaball
runners_data.note: Reserve runner with a single hurdle outing (pulled up over 2m2f on good ground); trainer Casey angle is unknown at this level and the single data point is not encouraging, pending any market move.

runners_data.name: Texas Red
runners_data.note: Reserve runner, unknown style, six-year-old with a placing at 3m on good ground in his history; if he runs, Rothwell's yard form needs monitoring, but the 39-day gap and modest form figures offer no strong case.

races.paceDynamic: Highland Realm is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner maiden hurdle and, with no genuine rival to press them from the off, Sean O'Keeffe can dictate a controlled, measured gallop around Wexford's turning track over 2m½f on good ground. Penny Express and Game Point are the likeliest prominent challengers to sit just behind, but neither has the pace profile to seriously disrupt Highland Realm's rhythm in the early stages. The field is saturated with hold-up types — Finjimk, Chasing Blues, Colwyn Bay, Among The Pines, Betterluckthistime and Blue Nude are all true hold-up horses who have been mapped to midfield simply because there is nowhere else to put them; of those, Chasing Blues (De Bromhead/D O'Keeffe) and Finjimk are most likely to secure a workable midfield berth, while others will be shuffled further back than ideal. A steady, front-runner-controlled tempo that only quickens from the second-last strongly favours prominent and early-travelling profiles — horses who can sit close enough to the pace to respond when the real race begins, without being caught in the traffic that a compressed hold-up group will generate late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Highland Realm Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Highland Realm is allowed to dictate a comfortable gallop and quickens from two out unchallenged.
scenarios.body: Highland Realm bowls along in front at a pace that suits them, and with no rival willing or able to press, the Mullins runner simply extends from the second-last and the hold-up brigade, stuck in traffic, cannot bridge the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Penny Express or Game Point tracks the pace closely enough to pounce when Highland Realm's stride shortens at the final flight.
scenarios.body: A steady pace plays into the hands of a well-placed prominent mover who is travelling within themselves until two out; Penny Express, with Jack Kennedy in the saddle and consistent placing form, is ideally suited to pouncing from second or third.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and a strong-finishing midfield type finds a clear run through a tiring field in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Chasing Blues, handled by Darragh O'Keeffe for De Bromhead and with hurdles form on good ground, is the best-credentialled of those mapped to midfield; if the early gallop is truly pedestrian and the field spreads out, a late surge becomes viable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically up the straight, gifting the genuine hold-up types a rare opportunity to reel in leaders.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on horses that are either redistributed from their natural style or carrying the fade-in-finish flag — making it the least likely shape to produce a winner; among those best-placed to capitalise if it does materialise, Pinkarizon and Among The Pines have each shown placed flat form suggesting residual ability.

watchPoints.text: Highland Realm is the only horse in the race capable of setting and controlling the pace — if Sean O'Keeffe gets a clear lead unchallenged, the race could be over as a contest from the second-last hurdle.

Jack Kennedy takes the ride on Penny Express for Gordon Elliott — a prominent racer with consistent placing form, and this jockey-trainer combination regularly activates in maiden hurdles where a patient stalk-and-pounce is possible.

The Rothwell yard has four runners (Colwyn Bay, Betterluckthistime, Blue Nude, Texas Red) — watch for an unexpected market move on any one of them in the ring, as stable intent could be concentrated on a single runner.

At least six genuine hold-up horses have been mapped into midfield due to overcrowding at the rear — expect significant traffic and shuffling from the fourth-last, which could trap several fancied runners and distort the result.

Drumconnor Hill's unknown style profile (U-tag) with a placed run last time deserves monitoring in the betting — if Collins targets this trip on good ground with a plan, the absence of a reliable style read makes it a potential dark horse.

races.name: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On August 29th Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Bold Reflection
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old prominent racer with a win on good ground at 2m and solid placed form; jockey Alex Harvey and trainer John McConnell combination worth noting, though recent form shows limited fire and she's winless over longer trips.|

runners_data.name: Lilannbee
runners_data.note: Won over 2m2f on good ground and has placed form on soft, making her the most respected hold-up performer here — her natural instinct is to come from off the pace but the crowded rear means she will likely race closer to midfield than ideal, tempering her finishing threat.|

runners_data.name: Are You Around
runners_data.note: Mullins runner with two placed runs on good ground including a second over 2m4f, the most relevant form profile in the field for this trip and surface; 272 days off is the main concern, though Mullins horses often return fresh.|

runners_data.name: Cailin Hill
runners_data.note: Moderate debut form (tenth over 2m), a hold-up type whose finishing tendency has already flagged as a fade; runs out of role closer to midfield given the congested rear and holds limited appeal at this level.|

runners_data.name: Jolly D'olivate
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old with a win on her profile but only a distant eighth on her single run at this going, and flagged as a fader — her natural position at the back of the field is compromised here, and a 9-day turnaround adds little confidence.|

runners_data.name: Louve d'Arc
runners_data.note: Three runs over hurdles with modest form (fourth best finish), a genuine hold-up horse whose best chance is a truly end-to-end gallop; 128 days off but not lightly raced enough to be a concern.|

runners_data.name: Lunar Majesty
runners_data.note: An OR-96 runner, notably the lowest-rated in the field, with six runs showing consistent mid-pack finishes on varying ground; racing out of her natural back-of-field position in this crowded field, she looks up against it on ratings alone.|

runners_data.name: Miss Jocund
runners_data.note: Five runs on good ground all delivering placed or near-placed finishes, making her the most consistent performer on today's surface; headgear noted, races with unknown style (U) but her consistency suggests she can follow the pace and grind out a result.|

runners_data.name: Red Sea Girl
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner and race-shaper — four runs on good ground with three placed finishes suggest she handles conditions well, but her STYLE_FIT flag is a reminder that sole lead over 2m4f in a 17-runner field is a demanding ask if she's a shade below peak.|

runners_data.name: Thesilverbridle
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with unknown going profile and a form string of F71 over hurdles; trainer McConnell double-handed today, 102 days off, and the fall on debut adds jumping reliability risk — genuine unknown quantity in a big field.|

runners_data.name: Urra Mass Rock
runners_data.note: Single hurdle start produced a last-place finish over 2m4f on good ground; the fading flag and hold-up style in a field this large makes it very hard to identify a route to competitiveness.|

runners_data.name: Burning Like Fire
runners_data.note: Only one hurdle run (third) and 116 days off; unknown going profile at this level for Denis Hogan's four-year-old, but the youth and freshness could make her unexpectedly dangerous if the race falls apart — the most interesting dark horse among the unknowns.|

runners_data.name: Gratitudeforgrace
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott sends out a four-year-old with a debut last-place finish over 2m; her natural hold-up profile gets shuffled closer to midfield in this crowded field, and while the trainer commands respect, the raw form asks for patience.|

runners_data.name: My Girl Rosie
runners_data.note: Three runs with modest placed form at best (fifth was best finish), a hold-up fader in a race where the rear is heavily congested — the 9-day turnaround and unspectacular form make her hard to assess positively.|

runners_data.name: Queenofqueenstreet
runners_data.note: 377 days off the track, a single last-place debut, and flagged as a fader — the layoff alone makes her a significant risk in a competitive 17-runner field, and Reserve 1 jockey allocation adds further uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: Tubberfinn Lassie
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old with two pulled-up runs and a tongue tie on record; 277 days off and unknown going profile, jockey Reserve 2 — almost impossible to assess with confidence and unlikely to feature.|

runners_data.name: Runaway Rosie
runners_data.note: Mullins runner but with a single last-place debut 318 days ago, jockey Reserve 3 — the trainer commands automatic respect but this is as lightly-exposed as it gets, and the layoff is substantial enough to expect rustiness.|

races.paceDynamic: Red Sea Girl is the single confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful challenger for the lead in a 17-runner mares' maiden hurdle over 2m4f on good ground at Wexford, she is likely to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. The prominent types — Bold Reflection and Are You Around — will sit just behind her, but neither is likely to apply serious pressure through the early and middle stages, meaning the pace will be honest rather than gruelling. Several genuine hold-up performers (Lilannbee, Cailin Hill, Jolly D'olivate, Lunar Majesty, Gratitudeforgrace) have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because the rear of the field is congested with closers who cannot all find their natural position; in practice, runners like Lilannbee and Gratitudeforgrace are most likely to actually navigate toward the front of that chasing group. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a fair clip over a strongly-run 2m4f trip — strongly favours horses able to race prominently or track the pace into the straight and sustain their effort, rather than late closers who need a truly hot pace to deliver their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Red Sea Girl Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Red Sea Girl bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair but manageable tempo that softens out the closers.
scenarios.body: Red Sea Girl dictates every yard from flag to finish, turning a stamina test into a controlled exercise that nullifies the hold-up brigade; horses able to track her — Bold Reflection, Are You Around — sit best placed to challenge from two out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Setters Fade, Trackers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Red Sea Girl's solo lead proves slightly too ambitious over 2m4f and she ties up in the final two flights.
scenarios.body: The pace-tracking prominent horses Bold Reflection and Are You Around inherit a race set up for those with the best reserves, with the Mullins runner Are You Around's class making her particularly dangerous in this situation.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is hot enough — or the leader makes a jumping error — to leave genuine ground-closers with a furlong of raw momentum.
scenarios.body: Lilannbee, racing closer to the pace than her natural hold-up style prefers due to redistribution, or Miss Jocund — who has shown consistent placed form on good ground — could pick off tired rivals in the closing stages if the fractions have been genuinely searching.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Large Field Upsets Pace
scenarios.trigger: If early scrimmaging in a 17-runner field disrupts the pace map entirely, causing a false pace or traffic problems that shuffle the order.
scenarios.body: An unknown or lightly raced runner — Burning Like Fire, Thesilverbridle — could emerge from the pack if the race becomes a scramble with multiple horses checking or losing rhythm at flights.

watchPoints.text: Red Sea Girl sets the entire race shape — if she jumps poorly at any flight or is pressed by Bold Reflection in the back straight, the tempo will spike sharply and bring the hold-up horses back into play far sooner than the map suggests.

Are You Around's 272-day absence is the most significant unknown in the race; Mullins runners often return ready, but if she needs the run she will drop away from a tracking position at a critical point and distort the shape behind her.

With 17 runners in a mares' maiden, traffic problems between the last two flights are a real risk — watch for Lilannbee and Miss Jocund being blocked if they try to deliver runs up the inner as the field fans out.

Burning Like Fire and Thesilverbridle are the two most genuinely unknown quantities — either could be well-handicapped debutants or point-to-point types operating above their level; watch for them travelling unusually well in the early stages as the clearest signal of dark-horse involvement.

The Reserve jockey slots for Queenofqueenstreet, Tubberfinn Lassie and Runaway Rosie mean confirmed rider changes are still possible close to race time — any upgrade to a leading conditional or senior jockey on one of these runners would be worth noting before betting.

races.name: Wexford Racecourse Ladies Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: An Peann Dearg
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Paul Nolan who has run twice recently at Good over shorter; form string shows P-P in last two, and at 9 years old on 168lbs, stamina is a factor but consistency is not.|

runners_data.name: Jonny Carrol
runners_data.note: Unclassified style adds uncertainty; 57 days off for Moses McCabe, but best form (3rd, 3rd) has come at 20-22f on Good or Heavy — the trip and going are squarely in her comfort zone.|

runners_data.name: Harpy Eagle
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner; R P Cody's 5-year-old carries a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 meaning she is technically racing outside her most effective profile, but the absence of any genuine pace rival means she will dictate regardless — jumping accuracy will be crucial.|

runners_data.name: Midleton Rare
runners_data.note: Has won over this exact 24f trip on Good for Noel C Kelly and finished fourth in the same conditions recently; 68 days off is worth monitoring, but the course-and-distance form makes her a legitimate prominent threat.|

runners_data.name: Costanuci
runners_data.note: John Queally's 9-year-old ran just 13 days ago and has solid Good-ground form over this trip; a natural prominent type who may find herself shuffled back further than ideal given the congested early order.|

runners_data.name: Sean Mc
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's 6-year-old has a win over 20f on Good and placed multiple times in similar conditions; prominent style and recent 54-day break are key notes, and his profile maps perfectly onto a steady-pace scenario.|

runners_data.name: Coolboy Christy
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell's 5-year-old carries a hold-up tag despite running prominently in past starts; T14 of 1/21 from a big team, ran 40 days ago, and hasn't threatened in good ground recently — consistency is the concern.|

runners_data.name: Empire Walk
runners_data.note: Ran third over 24f on Good just recently for J Motherway — the right trip and ground — and has a natural prominent style that could see her settle just behind the leaders in a sensible early order.|

runners_data.name: Double Power
runners_data.note: Donoghue's 6-year-old has been well beaten in each of the last two Good-ground runs; prominent style but recent form figures of 9 and 7 are discouraging, and the 17-day turnaround doesn't change the picture.|

runners_data.name: Matter Of Opinion
runners_data.note: 203 days off the track is a significant flag for William Harvey's mare; hold-up style means she needs a strong pace to get competitive, and the slow tempo projected here makes her task harder.|

runners_data.name: Je Suis
runners_data.note: Holds two recent 5th and 3rd places over 26f on Good for S Curling — she wants further than today's 2m4f ideally, but her hold-up style and stamina could see her stay on late; ran just 11 days ago.|

runners_data.name: Ladiam
runners_data.note: Norman Lee's 9-year-old is a genuine prominent racer by nature with solid Good-ground figures (1W, 6P over 22f), but the pace map has displaced her to midfield — her chance is real but contingent on getting closer to her natural position than the map allows.|

runners_data.name: Ocean Murphy
runners_data.note: The 4-year-old for P J Rothwell is the youngest in the field with an OR of 92; hold-up style, no wins recorded, and recent Good-ground form of 9th are not encouraging at this trip and level.|

runners_data.name: Stumblin In
runners_data.note: Jack Doyle's 7-year-old ran just 2 days ago — an extremely quick turnaround — and form figures on Good ground show her consistently finishing 6th to 13th; a natural hold-up type pushed to midfield on the map, but the back-to-back race angle is the dominant concern here.|

runners_data.name: Larkins Lane
runners_data.note: Rothwell's 7-year-old has back-to-back wins on Good and Soft over 20f, making her form the most compelling in the lower weights; she's a genuine front-running type whose position has been redistributed to midfield given the prominent traffic — if she can secure closer ground early, she becomes dangerous.|

runners_data.name: China Grill
runners_data.note: Evanna McCutcheon's 5-year-old carries a ⚠ fades-in-finish tag and has four consecutive 10th-or-worse finishes on Good; hold-up style displaced further forward on the map is irrelevant — the form and the fitness flag make her a non-factor.|

races.paceDynamic: Harpy Eagle is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner field and is likely to control proceedings from the front without any genuine challenger for the lead, setting a measured, sustainable gallop over 2m4f on Good ground. Behind her, Sean Mc, Midleton Rare, Costanuci, Empire Walk and Double Power all carry prominent running styles, but there are far more of these types than the race shape can accommodate — Sean Mc and Midleton Rare hold the strongest claims to secure close-up positions just off the pace, with Costanuci and Empire Walk likely to settle a little further back than ideal. Ladiam and Larkins Lane are genuine prominent types who have been redistributed to midfield on the pace map precisely because this field is overcrowded with forward-runners, meaning both will race out of their natural position and should be discounted in scenarios that require them to dictate. With a lone front-runner and an uncontested lead, this race shape strongly favours horses able to travel prominently or just off the leader without burning fuel, and who possess the class and jumping accuracy to sustain their effort from the second-last — a steady-pace scenario that suits established prominent racers over hold-up specialists, who face a stiff task generating momentum from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Harpy Eagle Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Harpy Eagle is allowed to bowl along in front without any rival forcing the tempo, turning the race into a jumping and stamina test.
scenarios.body: Harpy Eagle sets an honest but uncontested pace, and the horses who track her closely from the outset — Sean Mc and Midleton Rare — are perfectly placed to pounce from the second-last; the steady gallop rewards those with good jumping and proven form at this course and trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Outstay Prominent Pack
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group burns each other out jostling for position and a genuine stayer comes from off the pace.
scenarios.body: The cluster of prominent types creates enough competitive pressure in the final mile to blunt their finishing effort, opening the door for a horse who has relaxed midfield and travels strongly to the last; this distance and Good ground suits a stayer who has hit form over 2m4f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Harpy Eagle travels exceptionally well through the race and the pack fails to close the gap from the second-last.
scenarios.body: In a truly uncontested lead scenario on Good ground, a relaxed front-runner who jumps fluently can find reserves to hold rivals at bay up the straight; this outcome is more likely if the prominent types are slow to organise behind her.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Mover Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed types — Ladiam or Larkins Lane — defies their compromised position and produces an unexpectedly strong late run.
scenarios.body: Despite being forced further back than natural, a horse with a sharp recent performance and class advantage could still pick off tiring rivals in the straight; Larkins Lane's back-to-back wins give her the profile to do so if the pace collapses.

watchPoints.text: Harpy Eagle's jumping — as the lone front-runner she controls the race entirely, but any mistake at a hurdle could compress the field and produce a very different finish.|
The prominent pack of Sean Mc, Midleton Rare, Costanuci and Empire Walk all want similar real estate early — watch for a bunched, fractious early order that compromises one or more of their chances.|

Larkins Lane has been displaced from her natural prominent position on the pace map; if she manages to travel closer to the leaders than mapped, her recent winning form makes her a genuine threat to upset the expected order.|
Stumblin In ran just 2 days ago — monitor market support or absence of it at the off; a horse with back-to-back runs in 48 hours rarely improves and could be an early faller risk.|

Matter Of Opinion has been off 203 days and is a hold-up type in a race projected to run at a steady pace — the combination of layoff and race shape makes a winning performance highly unlikely on debut back.|

races.name: Cottage Autism Network Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Charlie's Dilemma
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race; John C McConnell's 7yo has Good-ground form at similar trips and sets his own fractions here, though recent finishes in the 7-8 range suggest limited acceleration and he is being asked to race from a slightly more forward role than his P-style implies — his chance depends entirely on the pace staying controlled.

runners_data.name: Jury Foreman
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's 5yo has a worrying 'U' in the form string and a 57-day absence; sim-going figures of 0W0P on Good offer little encouragement, and the trip looks a stretch for a horse rated 96 who has not been seen since pulling up — a difficult each-way proposition.

runners_data.name: Gerrys Wish
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy in the saddle is an immediate upgrade for Gordon Elliott's 5yo, who has genuine placed form at 24f on Good ground (back-to-back seconds); a prominent runner with strong credentials on this surface and a jockey who will place him perfectly tracking the leader.

runners_data.name: Barryroe Madam
runners_data.note: The most authentic hold-up horse in the field; Terence O'Brien's 7yo was placed at 24f on Good and won from this running style, but recent finishes of 0-0-0 since that Good-ground win are a significant concern over a sharp track like Wexford.

runners_data.name: John Storey
runners_data.note: Pulled up twice recently and absent 102 days; Ian Patrick Donoghue's 8yo wears a tp headgear combination and has struggled for fluency — the lay-off and stopping form make him a risky proposition in a 15-runner field over 3m.

runners_data.name: Ersudaly
runners_data.note: Colin Bowe's 6yo ran just 9 days ago and has 70F-70 in the form — the 'F' fall and repeated backend finishes are concerning; wears a hood but sim-going figures of just 3/6 on Good give no reason to think the surface brings out the best in him.

runners_data.name: Ellens Pride
runners_data.note: S Curling's 6yo is tagged as fading in the finish, and with a hood on and recent form of 21-04P, the early promise has not translated to 3m stamina — Phillip Enright must balance keeping him in contention while managing a horse who typically stops late.

runners_data.name: Ballinaboola Hanna
runners_data.note: Richard Deegan partners R Donohoe's 5yo returning after 100 days; sim-going figures of just 1/6 on Good are the worst in the field, suggesting this surface does not suit — the distance may also stretch her based on a form string showing no finish beyond 23f in win/place efforts.

runners_data.name: True Harmony
runners_data.note: Seamus Neville's 6yo is flagged as fading in the finish and carries a style-fit concern — though a true hold-up horse by nature, the congested rear of this field means she cannot settle in her preferred position; sim-going figures show 0W1P and the fade flag makes the 3m trip a significant question.

runners_data.name: Fervida
runners_data.note: Ross Berry (7) takes the mount for J A Berry's 6yo, who has a pattern of fading — P89P-9 with a sim-going record of 4/7 and no wins suggests this runner is competing at the limit of ability; the apprentice claim may offset weight but the profile is uninspiring over 3m.

runners_data.name: Katie's Casper
runners_data.note: Dermot McLoughlin's 7yo has quiet placed form at 24f on Good (two seconds in recent history) and tp headgear; though a hold-up horse by nature, the crowded rear of this field pushes her forward on the map — her best efforts have come when given time to build, and that may not be possible here.

runners_data.name: Lady Victrix
runners_data.note: 178 days off the track for Paul Flynn's 6yo, who fades in the finish and is a genuine hold-up runner forced into midfield by the congested field — that combination of a very long absence, fade flag, and compromised tactical position makes her extremely hard to support.

runners_data.name: Hob's Angel
runners_data.note: Donagh Meyler's 10yo won at 20f on Good recently and has a 1W3P sim-going record; a prominent runner whose durability over hurdles at this age is a genuine asset in a 15-runner field, and recent form of 06-125 shows he is in form heading into this race.

runners_data.name: Set The Tone
runners_data.note: David O'Brien's 5yo holds a second at 22f on Good in recent form (P8-0P2) and wears a tongue-tie; a true hold-up horse shuffled into midfield by the crowded field, his best result at this trip suggests he can stay — Conor Stone-Walsh should be alive to an opportunity if the race unravels late.

runners_data.name: Strong Contender
runners_data.note: Last ran just 2 days ago which is exceptionally quick for a hurdles horse, and Norman Lee's 5yo has a fade flag plus 0W1P on Good; a natural hold-up runner mapped to midfield, the ultra-short turnaround is the overriding concern here and will warrant close scrutiny before the off.

races.paceDynamic: Charlie's Dilemma is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner 3m handicap hurdle, and with no identified rivals willing to take him on from the front, he is set to control tempo from the outset at a pace he dictates himself. Gerrys Pride, John Storey, and Hob's Angel are the prominent-racing types most likely to sit just off Charlie's Dilemma, tracking him through the early and middle stages of a trip that rewards stamina and jumping economy. On Good ground over three miles at Wexford, a controlled, sustainable gallop suits horses that can travel prominently, jump cleanly, and pick up from a reasonable position entering the home straight — this race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent or close-tracking runners rather than hold-up types who will likely be making up ground from off the pace that was never truly strong enough to soften up the leaders. Several runners — True Harmony, Katie's Casper, Set The Tone, Lady Victrix, and Strong Contender — are genuine hold-up horses who have been mapped forward simply because the field contains too many rear-of-field types to all find their natural position; in reality, Hob's Angel and Gerrys Wish are best placed to actually secure a ground-saving pitch close to Charlie's Dilemma.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Charlie's Dilemma meets no pace pressure and dictates a measured, unchallenged gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Charlie's Dilemma bowls along in front setting a rhythm that drains stamina gradually rather than explosively, meaning those tracking him closely are best placed to pounce at the last hurdle; prominent types who can sit second or third without expending energy are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challengers Sweep Past
scenarios.trigger: If one or two close-tracking prominent runners measure their effort over 3m and overhaul Charlie's Dilemma from the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: A well-judged prominent ride, travelling within the leader's slipstream and easing to the front approaching the last, is the classic winning profile for this shape on Good ground at Wexford; Gerrys Wish's placed form at 24f on Good and Hob's Angel's recent win under similar conditions both suit this execution.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge Falls Short
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late enough that genuine hold-up horses can close ground but still face too much to make up.
scenarios.body: True Harmony, Katie's Casper, and Set The Tone are all natural closers but are mapped forward in this race — meaning they are unlikely to be in their true comfort zone, and any late run they produce is from a compromised position rather than a genuine hold-up berth; Barryroe Madam is the most authentic hold-up runner here and her Good-ground form gives her the best profile in this scenario, though her recent results make the ceiling modest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Race; Survivors Win
scenarios.trigger: If the field strings out over the 3m trip, errors and fatigue eliminate leading contenders, and a durable stayer picks through the wreckage.
scenarios.body: At 15 runners over 3 miles, jumping errors become a meaningful factor — John Storey and Jury Foreman have pulled-up form which raises questions, but a horse who jumps cleanly and stays honest through the last mile could inherit a placing; Hob's Angel's jumping record and recent course form give him durability claims if the race falls apart ahead of him.

watchPoints.text: Strong Contender ran just 2 days ago — monitor markets and any late jockey news as the Reserve 1 booking and rapid turnaround could signal a non-runner or a horse that is not fully ready.

John Storey has pulled up in two of his last five starts and returns from 102 days off — if he jumps poorly early in a 15-runner field, he becomes an obstacle risk that could affect horses tracking him.

Gerrys Wish's chance is closely tied to Jack Kennedy settling him immediately behind Charlie's Dilemma — if Kennedy is forced wide or cannot find a prominent pitch in a large field, his ground-saving ability is compromised from the outset.

Hob's Angel's age (10) makes it worth watching how fluently he jumps in the early stages — his recent win is form-positive but a 3m Wexford trip over hurdles tests jumping accuracy at a track that can catch older horses out.

Ballinaboola Hanna and Lady Victrix are both long-absent hold-up types (100 and 178 days respectively) — watch the market for either; significant support for a returning horse of this profile in a 15-runner handicap could be informative, but their absence and fade flags warrant caution.

races.name: Cottage Autism Network Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Desert Cave
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 98 and a natural hold-up horse who stays well; Rian Lane (7) takes off 7lbs, and his similar-going record of 11 runs at 1W2P on Good suggests he handles conditions — the step up to 3m is the key question given his recent form has been over shorter.|

runners_data.name: Moonlight Paradise
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan-trained 5yo whose flat-out hold-up style suits a patient ride; best form came when finishing 4th on Good ground over 20f but a 0W0P record on similar going and a pulled-up last time out makes confidence hard to muster despite Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim.|

runners_data.name: Georgia Celena
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner and effectively the pace anchor for this race; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) tempers her win chance slightly as this is not her natural dominant role, but her 13/15 similar-going record shows she handles the conditions and she gets a handy weight at 157lbs.|

runners_data.name: Fire Coral
runners_data.note: Outstanding Good-ground performer with a 15/15 similar-going record, two wins at comparable distances, and Phillip Enright — an experienced jockey — in the saddle; a natural prominent type at OR 88 with a recent 3rd to back it up, and the hg:t (tongue-tie) is presumably working.|

runners_data.name: Nashville Notions
runners_data.note: Hold-up style and 48 days since last run are minor concerns, but a win at OR 88 on Good ground and a decent 5/22f Good run in the book give hope over this stamina test; form tailed off badly in the past two (PU and 0) so needs to rediscover that earlier level.|

runners_data.name: Keep The Head
runners_data.note: Carries a "fades in finish" flag which is damaging over 3m, and a 68-day absence compounds the worry; OR 84 and a 0W0P similar-going record mean there is little in the data to get excited about, even with Darragh O'Keeffe's experience in the saddle.|

runners_data.name: Chasing Crowns
runners_data.note: Blinkers applied and a genuine hold-up horse at heart — the redistribution to midfield reflects that the map cannot place all deep runners at the rear, not his preferred racing style; the "fades in finish" tag over 3m is a real concern, and a 0W1P similar-going record at OR 83 offers limited appeal.|

runners_data.name: Trixaboutmaisie
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type whose recent form (870-7) reads poorly, and all four of his similar-going runs have resulted in finishes of 4th or worse with no wins or places; Colin Bowe sends him out only 9 days after his last run — that freshness angle aside, his profile at OR 83 gives little encouragement.|

runners_data.name: Urbs Intacta Manet
runners_data.note: Carries both a "fades in finish" warning and a 71-day layoff, which is a double flag over 3m; a natural hold-up horse pushed to midfield on the map, his similar-going record reads just 2 from 6 with 0W0P and a form string of 0P06-0 — hard to make a case.|

runners_data.name: Ballinaboola Gold
runners_data.note: Showed a promising 2nd over 24f on Good ground in his last five runs and Richard Deegan takes the ride; a true hold-up horse whose map position doesn't reflect his natural style, but the hg:p headgear and a 6/12 similar-going record with 0W1P suggest he's capable of a better run than his 08-257 form implies.|

runners_data.name: Talas Kera
runners_data.note: Placed twice at this trip or near it on Good ground (4/24f, 3/16f) so the stamina angle is there; Eoghan Finegan (5) claims 5lbs and the 7/9 similar-going record is solid for the level, though being a natural hold-up horse repositioned to midfield means he'll need things to fall right.|

runners_data.name: Clever Court
runners_data.note: Recent winner (1 from 1 on Good ground over 20f) who wears blinkers and is ridden by Shane O'Callaghan (3) for a trainer with a positive recent profile; a natural prominent type at OR 78 whose fresh form and headgear suggest he'll race with intent — stamina over 3m is the one unknown.|

runners_data.name: Phildante
runners_data.note: A 9yo prominent-style horse at OR 75 with tongue-tie and a pads combination, and his form of 06-64F includes a fall last time — jumping safety is a watch point; decent 4/20f and 6/22f Good-ground placings are in the book but no wins in 15 similar-going runs tells its own story.|

runners_data.name: Cruisin Susan
runners_data.note: Carries a "fades in finish" tag which is a major issue at 3m; a natural hold-up horse placed in midfield on the map for structural reasons, and a 55-day absence plus 0W1P from 15 similar-going runs at OR 72 means she would need a significant step forward.|

runners_data.name: Glaoinn An Airgead
runners_data.note: Reserve rider listed and a 0W0P record from 15 similar-going runs tells you everything you need to know about the prospects here at OR 72; a true hold-up horse repositioned to midfield on the map, and a form string of 5F0-0P with a fall in there makes jumping confidence a valid concern.|

races.paceDynamic: Georgia Celena is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner field and, with no other natural leader likely to press her hard from the outset, she should control proceedings at a measured, sustainable gallop over this 3m trip on Good ground at Wexford. Fire Coral and Clever Court will look to track closely from prominent positions, with Phildante also likely to race nearer the pace, meaning the front section will have some company but no genuine pressure source to force an honest tempo. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Trixaboutmaisie, Chasing Crowns, Urbs Intacta Manet, Ballinaboola Gold, Talas Kera, Glaoinn An Airgead, and Cruisin Susan are all natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield positions because the map cannot place them all at the rear; of those, Trixaboutmaisie and Chasing Crowns are most likely to actually secure a prominent midfield berth given their recent form patterns. A controlled, front-runner-dictated race over 3m on Good ground at Wexford strongly favours prominently-raced horses with proven stamina at the trip — horses that can travel in behind the leader without being buried deep in the pack and pounce in the home straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Georgia Celena Dictates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Georgia Celena is allowed to control the pace entirely unchallenged and the field fails to reel her in up the straight.
scenarios.body: Georgia Celena sets a comfortable gallop, the strong hold-up bias in the field means few rivals can mount a sustained challenge from deep, and the race becomes a test of who has tracked closest throughout; Fire Coral and Clever Court, both natural prominent types with Good-ground form, are ideally placed to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely too slow early, creates a cavalry charge finish, and a horse from deep delivers a sustained run from the second-last.
scenarios.body: A dawdling tempo compresses the field approaching the final two hurdles, allowing a horse that has avoided trouble in midfield to produce a strong finishing run on the flat; Desert Cave and Moonlight Paradise, the two highest-rated hold-up types with proven Good-ground form at similar trips, are best positioned to benefit from this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to string the field out and a prominent-tracking horse proves the strongest stayer in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Fire Coral's outstanding similar-going record (15 from 15 on Good) and two wins at comparable distances make it the standout candidate if stamina is tested properly; Clever Court's recent win and blinkered headgear suggest it will be ridden positively and could outlast rivals who fade in the home straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Georgia Celena sets a falsely fast early gallop, capitulates before the last, and the race dissolves into a scramble up the straight.
scenarios.body: A pace collapse would open the door for horses that have raced economically in the body of the field; Nashville Notions and Ballinaboola Gold, both lightly raced at the trip with decent Good-ground profiles, could benefit from the resulting lottery, though neither is a standout selection in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Georgia Celena sets the pace unchallenged — watch whether Patrick M O'Brien (5) allows her to coast at a crawl or pushes on enough to test the field's stamina, as the tempo she sets will determine whether prominent or hold-up types benefit.|

Fire Coral's 15/15 similar-going Good-ground record stands out sharply in this field — watch to see that Phillip Enright positions it close enough to Georgia Celena to avoid being caught in a compressed finish, as it is the form benchmark for this race shape.|

Several runners carry "fades in finish" flags over 3m — Keep The Head, Chasing Crowns, Urbs Intacta Manet, and Cruisin Susan — watch the field closely after the last for potential fallers or horses stopping sharply, which could create interference for those tracking behind.|

Clever Court won last time out and wears blinkers — watch whether the headgear keeps it focused jumping in a big field of 15, as a prominently raced horse losing concentration at a hurdle early in the race would be a significant tactical setback.|

Glaoinn An Airgead has a reserve rider listed — watch for any late jockey change that could affect tactics, and note that a fall in recent form makes it a potential jumping hazard in a 15-runner field at a tight track like Wexford.|

races.name: Park Run At Wexford Saturday Mornings Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Duke Otto
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with winning form on Good at similar distances; 154 days off the track is a query but Patrick J Flynn has him fit enough to run, and sim-going record of 1W4P from 10 is respectable — best hope is a strong pace that strings the field out.

runners_data.name: Rightfolksplease
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner but alarmingly has not raced in 537 days; on a positive note he handles Good ground well (12/15 sim-going) and wears tongue-tie, and if fitness holds he sets every parameter of this race — Style Fit tag (0.91) reflects some positional uncertainty on reappearance.

runners_data.name: Boola Times
runners_data.note: Hold-up type prone to fading in the finish, which is a real concern in a race likely to be run at a measured pace; 98 days off and only one placed run in 13 sim-going starts leaves him needing everything to go right.

runners_data.name: Hatfield Hammer
runners_data.note: Prominent traveller trained by Paul Nolan who ran just 20 days ago and showed form over Good ground repeatedly in his hist; sim-going record of 1W7P from 14 is outstanding and he figures prominently under any scenario where the pace stays honest.

runners_data.name: Bella Union
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-style operator for John McConnell with two recent wins on Good and three placed efforts from 14 sim-going starts; 20-day turnaround is no concern given that record, and at OR 87 with 155lbs she looks well-treated in this company.

runners_data.name: Ranting And Raven
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Gavin Cromwell with a preference for prominent racing noted in headgear; only four years old in a largely older field and has yet to win, with no better than sixth in sim-going last five — likely needs improvement.

runners_data.name: Davitts Quay
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type who fades in finishes and has a 0W0P record in three sim-going starts — the form string of 070-0 offers little hope and he is at risk of being caught in traffic with so many hold-up horses unable to get their position.

runners_data.name: Cinnabar Moth
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose true rear-dwelling style cannot be accommodated in this congested field, forcing him forward against his nature; five runs on Good without a win and the Style Fit flag (0.90) adds to concerns about how much he can do racing out of his comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Backinabit
runners_data.note: Has a recent win on Good to his name and wears blinkers, giving him a respectable angle; however, he is a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield role by the field composition, and the fade-in-finish flag combined with Style Fit (0.92) means his best form requires conditions that won't materialise here.

runners_data.name: Mount Hotham
runners_data.note: Consistent back-marker who has finished in the bottom half of every recent run, and the combination of a fade-in-finish flag, no wins in sim-going, and being forced to race closer than ideal makes him one of the least likely winners in the field.

runners_data.name: Sidiriya
runners_data.note: Prominent-leaning type for P J Rothwell who has placed twice in sim-going from six starts; decent recent form of 306-32 and Darragh O'Keeffe in the saddle is an upgrade — will track the leaders and could make a bold bid if the pace doesn't quicken sharply.

runners_data.name: I'm For Home
runners_data.note: Kevin Healy takes the ride on this genuine hold-up horse who has been pushed into a midfield map position by field congestion; one placed run in seven sim-going starts and 76 days off the track make him a tough sell, and racing out of his natural style caps his ceiling.

runners_data.name: Esticky End
runners_data.note: Prominent-style operator who was placed last time out and handles Good ground on a consistent basis; Dylan Robinson takes the ride and at OR 73 with 141lbs the light weight helps, though the form string of 55-7P2 suggests placed efforts rather than winning ones.

races.paceDynamic: Rightfolksplease is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with 537 days off the track, will likely be allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a sustainable clip on Good ground over 2m½f at Wexford. Hatfield Hammer, Bella Union, and Sidiriya will press forward prominently but none are natural tearaway types, meaning the pace is unlikely to be punishing — Rightfolksplease should control tempo without being seriously pressured into the back straight. The field carries a significant cluster of genuine hold-up horses — Cinnabar Moth, Backinabit, Mount Hotham, and I'm For Home — none of whom will be able to settle into their true rear position given how many share that profile, forcing them to race closer than ideal and compromising their finishing kicks. This race shape squarely favours prominent-to-handy riders who can track the honest lead at a controlled pace and produce a well-timed challenge from second or third — horses like Bella Union and Hatfield Hammer are ideally positioned to exploit a tempo that will never become truly searching.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Rightfolksplease sets a fair but unspectacular gallop and the prominent types track smoothly into contention from 3 out.
scenarios.body: Bella Union and Hatfield Hammer, both handy-travelling types with solid Good-ground form, receive a perfect tow into the race and have enough in reserve to assert from the second-last; Bella Union's two recent wins on Good ground give her strong claims here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If Rightfolksplease, returning from 537 days off, settles into an uncontested rhythm and simply outstays rivals who are all racing out of position.
scenarios.body: With nothing to seriously push the pace, Rightfolksplease can find a comfortable cruising speed and the combination of no pressure plus Good ground allows him to idle to the line; the prominent types who track him lack the finishing acceleration to reel him in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and one true closer manages to find clear running late in the straight.
scenarios.body: Duke Otto, a hold-up type with winning form in similar going at this trip, is the most plausible beneficiary if gaps open; however, the redistribution of multiple hold-up horses forward means the late-run scenario is structurally compromised as the rear of the field lacks true closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace fractures mid-race — Rightfolksplease stops suddenly on his comeback and multiple horses check, causing a scrambled finish.
scenarios.body: Backinabit, who has a win in recent form and blinkers on, could pounce opportunistically in the melee; Esticky End, placed recently and racing prominently, could also benefit from confusion at the head of affairs.

watchPoints.text: Bella Union has back-to-back wins on Good and prominent style perfectly suits this controlled-pace shape — watch for her to travel smoothly in Hatfield Hammer's slipstream and quicken from the second-last.

Rightfolksplease is the pace-setter returning from 537 days off; if he fades abruptly in the home straight the whole race shape collapses and a chaotic finish could follow — monitor his jumping and early travelling.

Cinnabar Moth, Backinabit, Mount Hotham, and I'm For Home are all genuine hold-up horses crammed into a midfield role — watch for traffic issues and interference between these four as they jostle for positions they cannot naturally secure.

Hatfield Hammer ran 20 days ago and has a remarkable 1W7P record in sim-going from 14 starts — the freshness angle is fine and if Bella Union underperforms he is the most likely alternative prominent-style winner.

Sidiriya with Darragh O'Keeffe is an interesting place claim if the pace stays honest — two placed efforts in sim-going and a recent form figure of 32 suggest he is coming into form at the right time.

races.name: Park Run At Wexford Saturday Mornings Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Del Boys Diva
runners_data.note: Shane Crawley's 6yo has winning form on Good (1 win, 1 place from 5 similar-going runs) and Sean O'Keeffe rides; a confirmed hold-up type who tends to fade late so needs the pace to soften rivals before she strikes, and 17 days between runs looks fine.|

runners_data.name: Tropical Twist
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy adds significant jockey quality for Gordon Elliott who has 9 winners from 48 over 14 days; hold-up in style, has finished 5th on Good ground twice and lacks a recent win but the booking is eye-catching.|

runners_data.name: Glendower
runners_data.note: Eoin Doyle's 5yo is a hold-up type who has placed 4 times in 15 similar-going runs without winning; Paddy Cody takes off 7lbs which is significant at this level, and the horse has course-type experience on Good.|

runners_data.name: Let It Settle
runners_data.note: A horse with a fade warning who has finished 2nd on Good ground once but has also pulled up and trailed in large fields; Harry Sexton's 7lb claim eases the burden but the pattern of stopping in the finish is a consistent concern over this trip.|

runners_data.name: Victoria Kesia
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's 5yo is a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position has been absorbed by the sheer volume of closers in the field, placing her in midfield on the map but unlikely to race there naturally; best effort was a 3rd on Good over a longer trip, and Donagh Meyler knows the yard.|

runners_data.name: Polly Poppins
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here with 5 of 5 career runs on Good ground (including this course), giving Tiernan Power Roche a clear mandate to bowl along; raced just 1 day ago which is an unusually short turnaround and merits monitoring, though she has placed twice from this position.|

runners_data.name: Eastern Blue Bird
runners_data.note: Richard Condon's 5lb claim softens the weight for P A Fahy's horse, which is a true hold-up type whose shorter-trip form on Good produced a 5th; placed into a midfield mapping due to the volume of closers, though getting a prominent berth here is unlikely given her natural style.|

runners_data.name: Syosset
runners_data.note: John McConnell's 5yo has a fade warning and wears headgear (h); most of her best form has come on Standard artificial surfaces (3 wins/places) rather than Good turf, and though she showed a 3rd on Good over 16f the style-fit discount is real given she's a true hold-up horse crammed into midfield.|

runners_data.name: Light Her Up
runners_data.note: Hugh Paul Finegan's 8yo was out just 2 days ago — a very short turnaround — and carries the tongue-strap and blinkers; form on Good ground is moderate (7th best finish in 9 similar-going runs) and her true hold-up style is compromised by the overcrowded rear of this field.|

runners_data.name: Liss Eile
runners_data.note: G Ahern's 6yo carries a veil and fade warning, and her 15 similar-going runs have produced just 1 placing at a finishing position of 10th on average; Darragh O'Keeffe is a capable jockey but the horse's profile offers little encouragement at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Tasmanian Girl
runners_data.note: 57 days off the track for Declan Queally's 6yo, who wears a tongue-strap; one win came on Good ground but it was in a very small field, and the fresher body may suit though she's a true hold-up horse redistributed into midfield — her last run was a pull-up.|

runners_data.name: Avandra
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell sends out this 6yo with Shane O'Callaghan's 3lb claim making her one of the lightest-weighted horses in the race at 145lbs; a 2nd on Good over 16f is her best effort, and she's a genuine hold-up type placed artificially into midfield — the claim and the light weight are her most credible angles.|

races.paceDynamic: Polly Poppins is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner handicap hurdle and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she is set to dictate at a sustainable gallop on Good ground around Wexford's right-handed circuit. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly hold-up in profile, meaning the tempo is unlikely to be pressured and Polly Poppins could control fractions freely from the front. This uncontested lead on a track that does not overly punish front-runners on Good ground sets up a race where prominent racers and those able to travel close to the pace without burning energy will be best positioned approaching the final hurdle. The field holds significantly more genuine hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Victoria Kesia, Syosset, Eastern Blue Bird, Liss Eile, Tasmanian Girl, Light Her Up, and Avandra are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield slots; of these, the most likely to actually secure a forward midfield berth are Avandra (light weight, 3lb claimer) and Eastern Blue Bird (has tracked prominent in shorter-trip races). A sustainable pace set by a lone leader on a flat, right-handed track with a modest field of closers stacked behind her unambiguously favours runners able to sit second or third and pounce from a stalking position rather than those finishing off a true test from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Polly Poppins Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Polly Poppins is allowed to bowl along at her own rhythm and the hold-up pack cannot muster a sustained challenge from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Polly Poppins sets a measured pace the whole field must run to catch, and with no prominent rival to push her through the early stages she conserves enough energy to see out the 2m½f trip; the Good ground suits her proven course profile (5 of last 5 runs on Good).

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalker Pounces Off Slow Pace
scenarios.trigger: If one of the horses immediately tracking Polly Poppins travels fluently and produces a sharp move from the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: The uncontested gallop compresses the field, allowing a well-placed stalker to strike at the business end before the true hold-up horses can gather momentum from further back; the Good surface rewards clean jumping and positive riding rather than a grind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Finisher Threads Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely muddling and the hold-up pack finds a clear run from two out to close down a tiring leader.
scenarios.body: A slowly-run race paradoxically helps a horse with a high cruising speed that can generate a late burst, but most of the redistriubuted hold-up types here carry style-fit discounts and face traffic risks in a bunched field; the scenario is possible but requires Polly Poppins to stop suddenly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Polly Poppins sets a false dawdle that causes the entire field to bunch and produces a chaotic sprint to the line.
scenarios.body: With 12 runners funnelling off a slow pace, interference and jumping errors become more likely, opening the door for a well-handicapped horse with a fresh body to steal it in the scramble; this scenario suits horses with strong finishing form and capable jockeys rather than the pace shape itself.

watchPoints.text: Polly Poppins ran just 1 day ago — monitor market moves and any late jockey or vet checks, as a horse this fresh off a recent run dictating pace throughout a 2m½f hurdle is a physical ask.
Jack Kennedy's booking for Tropical Twist (Elliott yard, 9/48 in 14 days) is above-average for this grade — watch for this horse drifting or shortening sharply in the market as a stable indicator.

With 7 genuine hold-up horses forced into a congested midfield behind a lone front-runner, traffic interference at the second-last hurdle is a serious risk — any horse needing a clear run from the rear could be badly hampered.

Avandra's 3lb claim at 145lbs gives her a significant weight advantage over the top weights and she showed a 2nd on Good ground over this sort of trip — watch whether the market reflects this booking for P J Rothwell.

Glendower and Let It Settle both carry 7lb claims (Cody and Sexton respectively) — if the pace is truly slow and the race becomes a sprint from the last, the lighter-burdened horses have a mechanical edge worth tracking.

races.name: Save The Date Ladies Day At Wexford Races Friday 7th August Flat Race
